primary_citation.popular_name: Business Records Exception to Hearsay — the exception that allows records kept in the regular course of business into evidence if foundation requirements are met

structural_location.chapter: CHAPTER 2. Exceptions to the Hearsay Rule [1220 - 1390]
structural_location.section_history: Enacted by Stats. 1965, Ch. 299. Amended by Stats. 2006, Ch. 69, Sec. 20.

verbatim_text.verbatim_full: Evidence of a writing made as a record of an act, condition, or event is not made inadmissible by the hearsay rule when offered to prove the act, condition, or event if: (a) The writing was made in the regular course of a business; (b) The writing was made at or near the time of the act, condition, or event; (c) The custodian or other qualified witness testifies to its identity and the mode of its preparation; and (d) The sources of information and method and time of preparation were such as to indicate its trustworthiness.

structural_breakdown.preamble: Evidence of a writing made as a record of an act, condition, or event is not made inadmissible by the hearsay rule — like § 1280, this exception removes the hearsay bar but does not eliminate the authentication requirement under §§ 1400-1401.
structural_breakdown.requirement_a: (a) The writing was made in the regular course of a business — the record must be a routine business record, not a document created specifically for litigation or for some purpose outside the business's normal operations. 'Business' is broadly defined to include any organization, profession, occupation, or calling of any kind.
structural_breakdown.requirement_b: (b) The writing was made at or near the time of the act, condition, or event — contemporaneity requirement, same principle as § 1280(b). Records created long after the events they purport to record do not qualify.
structural_breakdown.requirement_c: (c) The custodian or other qualified witness testifies to its identity and the mode of its preparation — the foundation witness requirement. Someone familiar with the business's record-keeping system must testify about what the record is and how it was created. This is a live-testimony requirement that cannot be waived.
structural_breakdown.requirement_d: (d) The sources of information and method and time of preparation were such as to indicate its trustworthiness — the trustworthiness gate, parallel to § 1280(c). Even records made in the regular course of business can be excluded if the circumstances indicate they are untrustworthy.
structural_breakdown.doctrinal_significance: § 1271 is the California business records exception to the hearsay rule. It governs the admissibility of financial records, medical billing records, employment records, transaction logs, and all other records kept in the regular course of any business. The four-part foundation requirement — regular course, contemporaneity, custodian testimony, and trustworthiness — must be satisfied by the proponent. Unlike § 1280 (official records), § 1271 requires a live custodian witness.

amendment_history.event: Original enactment as part of the 1965 Evidence Code recodification.
Technical amendment. The 2006 change was part of a non-substantive revision bill and did not alter the operative requirements of the section.

steward_case_relevance_audit.purpose: § 1271 governs the admissibility of every business record in the steward's case — medical billing records, financial transaction records, insurance records, debt collection records, employment records, phone company records. The custodian-witness requirement means that records offered without a qualified witness laying the foundation are inadmissible. The trustworthiness requirement means that records created under circumstances indicating unreliability can be challenged.

factor_audits.what_the_statute_requires: All four § 1271 requirements must be met for financial records to be admissible.
factor_audits.what_the_record_shows: The 19 unsigned documents in the Honeysuckle sale, the $72K crypto transactions, and the $25K surgery payment records must each independently qualify under § 1271. If the custodian cannot testify to the mode of preparation, or if the circumstances indicate the records were altered or created outside the regular course of business, the exception fails.
factor_audits.audit_status: CRITICAL — financial records are the backbone of the property fraud claims.

factor_audits.what_the_statute_requires: Medical billing records must be made in the regular course of the medical business, at or near the time of the service, with a custodian who can testify to the system.
factor_audits.what_the_record_shows: The spine surgery billing records ($35K), the SIRVA treatment records, and other medical records must qualify under § 1271. Records with billing code inconsistencies, services billed but not rendered, or records maintained by a system with documented unreliability fail the trustworthiness requirement.
factor_audits.audit_status: CRITICAL — medical billing fraud claims depend on showing that records fail § 1271's trustworthiness test.

factor_audits.what_the_statute_requires: A debt buyer's records must independently qualify under § 1271. The debt buyer cannot rely on the original creditor's business records foundation — the debt buyer must establish its own.
factor_audits.what_the_record_shows: Per Midland Funding v. Romero, debt collection records offered by a party that did not create the original records require an independent § 1271 foundation. The $19,985 Jaguar debt collection must be evaluated: does the collecting entity have a custodian who can testify to the mode of preparation of the records it relies on?
factor_audits.audit_status: CRITICAL — debt collection records are vulnerable to § 1271 challenges.

factor_audits.what_the_statute_requires: Treasury Department records may qualify under either § 1271 (business records) or § 1280 (official records), depending on the agency's characterization.
factor_audits.what_the_record_shows: The four contradictory Treasury responses about securities in the steward's name raise trustworthiness questions under both § 1271 and § 1280. Records that contradict each other from the same agency fail the trustworthiness test.
factor_audits.audit_status: RELEVANT — contradictory records from the same source undermine trustworthiness under either exception.

steward_case_relevance_audit.audit_summary: § 1271 is the foundation for every business record in the steward's case. Financial records, medical billing records, debt collection records, and insurance records must all pass the four-part test. The custodian-witness requirement and the trustworthiness gate are the two primary challenge points.

governing_guidelines.evidence: Cal. Evid. Code § 1271 is binding California state authority.
